title: Redwood cost-econ discovery with Pinelake Capital
summary: Initial cost/unit economics discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs. Pinelake is evaluating per-token pricing, batching/caching levers, and quantization options to meet a hard budget for an H2 pilot. Key concerns: predictable unit cost at peak, latency SLOs for trader-facing features, data residency and KMS for models. Agreed next steps: share cost model spreadsheet, schedule technical deep dive benchmark with Priya and Ethan, and send security docs and sample SLA for Dedicated.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private economics
next_steps: Redwood to share cost-model spreadsheet and pricing examples (Samira)
Schedule technical benchmark / deep dive with Priya and Ethan (Ethan to propose times)
Send SOC 2 / security and KMS integration docs (Samira)
Pinelake to provide sample prompt mix and expected QPS for pilot
action_items: Samira Patel; Share cost-model spreadsheet and sample pricing scenarios; 2026-03-09
Ethan Cole; Propose 2x timeslots for deep dive + benchmarking; 2026-03-06
Priya Nair (Pinelake); Send sample prompt mix and 1-week request trace; 2026-03-08
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Pinelake - Head Eng), Priya Nair (Pinelake - ML Infra Lead), Oliver Grant (Pinelake - CTO)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we know you had some background info in the deck, today we wanted to focus on the cost economics piece and how that maps to hosted vs dedicated vs private, quick intros?
[00:12] Marcus: yeah hi i'm Marcus, head of eng at Pinelake, we run a bunch of quant models and are looking to add LLM features for trader assist, latency is pretty important for us, budget even more, so main Q is how do we get predictable unit costs, and where are the biggest levers
[00:30] Priya: hi all, priya here, i'll be running infra for any pilot, we care about throughput and also about caching and KV implementation cause our prompts have heavy prefixes
[00:42] Ethan: great, im ethan, i'm the se on this, we'll dig into batching, kv cache and quantization tradeoffs. small note, sometimes transcription's off so bear with typos in the notes

[01:05] Samira: quick framing — Redwood's pricing for hosted is per-token with volume tiers, dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit and lower unit cost at scale, private is a license + infra ops. For cost-econ we usually model per-inference token cost, effective cost after batching and cache hits, and reserved amortization for dedicated.
[01:35] Marcus: can you run an example? like if we have 200k requests/day, average 120 tokens generated, what's per-token look like?
[01:48] Samira: sure, ballpark: hosted per-token might be $0.0009/1k tokens at low tier — sorry that's a bad example, let me be concrete — for text-gen hosted list price $0.002 per 1k output tokens at entry, with volume it moves down. so raw math: 200k reqs * 120 tokens = 24M tokens. at $0.002/1k -> $48/day. but that ignores batching and cache.
[02:30] Priya: wait that seems low? are we mixing output vs input tokens, and what about prompt cost? Our prompts are 800-1200 tokens often
[02:40] Samira: good catch — you're right. total tokens = prompt + response. so if prompt avg 900 and response 120, that's 1,020 tokens per call -> 204M tokens/day -> at $0.002 per 1k that's $408/day or like $12k/month, roughly. but with batching and prefix cache we can shave a lot off the effective output because same prompt prefixes repeated across traders, caching prevents re-executing the prefix.
[03:12] Ethan: technical aside — our KV/prefix caching means if 60% of token work is prefix we can avoid recomputing it for cached contexts, effective token billing still counts generated tokens but compute cost drops; for dedicated we can enable aggressive batching which reduces per-token unit since GPU throughput improves with larger batches. Also quantization to int8 or 4-bit can increase throughput and reduce infra cost but may slightly affect quality.
[03:47] Oliver: what's the typical hit rate you see on prefix cache? real world numbers?
[03:52] Ethan: it varies a lot — for comms with many repeated prefixes you can get 40-60% hit rates. for trading prompts where each query slightly differs, maybe 20-30%. we usually model conservative 25% hit as a start unless Pinelake can provide prompt mix.

[04:20] Marcus: ok so what would dedicated look like pricing wise? we want predictability during market hours
[04:27] Samira: Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity. For example a dedicated pool with 8x A100-equivalent GPUs might be a mid-size commit -> translates to a fixed monthly commit (we give numbers in the spreadsheet), and you get much lower per-token effective cost during high-throughput windows plus predictable latency. It also comes with options for burst capacity.
[04:52] Priya: and private? if our compliance needs force us on VPC or on-prem how different are the economics?
[04:58] Samira: Private has platform fee + customer infra. So infra spend is on you (or your cloud), license fee replaces some unit usage fees; net cost often higher for small scale but can be competitive if you have spare large-scale infra and need strict residency/KMS control.

[05:30] [05:30] Marcus: what about SLOs — can we keep tail latency under 200ms?
[05:36] Ethan: for short responses we can target sub-200ms with optimized runtimes and pinned models on dedicated. Hosted can hit similar medians but tails are less predictable unless you opt for dedicated. Caching helps tail too because cached paths skip heavy compute.

[06:10] Marcus: how do you model amortization? we want to allocate cost across teams and HAVE predictable unit cost even if usage is spiky during market open
[06:18] Samira: good Q. in the cost-model we amortize reserved capacity across expected QPS and usage hours — you can choose to amortize only market-hours (e.g., 8am-6pm) which yields lower effective per-token during those hours but higher off-hour effective cost. We also show a blended model: base reserved commit + overage per token.

[06:50] Priya: in practice, to get the benefit of batching, we need to control client concurrency patterns, is that something you recommend we do on our side?
[06:59] Ethan: yes, shaping client side concurrency into micro-batches works — Redwood's client SDK supports request coalescing and dynamic batching. We often advise a small proxy at the edge to aggregate requests during high throughput.

[07:25] Oliver: quantization — do you support mixed precision and how often do customers see quality regressions?
[07:33] Ethan: we support int8 and 4-bit quant paths for many models; quality regressions are workload dependent. we run evals on your prompt set to measure delta and pick the highest compression without significant regression. usually 8-bit is safe, 4-bit needs evals.

[08:05] [08:05] Marcus: competitors — we already trialed OpenAI for prototypes and looked at Vertex; cost was variable and unpredictable at spike times. any notes for comparisons?
[08:16] Samira: short: hosted Redwood aims to be price-competitive with a simpler SLA; Dedicated gets you more predictability vs OpenAI's pay-as-you-go; Vertex has integrated cloud benefits but less batching/kv tailoring out of the box. we'll include a short competitor comparison in the sheet.

[09:00] Priya: can you walk me through a sample row in the cost model spreadsheet? what inputs do you need from us?
[09:07] Samira: sure — inputs: avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens, requests per second (QPS) by hour, percent of repeated prefixes (cache hit estimate), percent of calls that can be batched, desired latency SLO, and pilot duration. From that we produce hosted per-month, dedicated commit size + amortized per-token, and private license + infra estimate.
[09:38] Priya: we can provide a week of real traces from our staging logs, would that be enough?
[09:43] Ethan: yes that's ideal — request traces with timestamps, prompt lengths, and any grouping key helps us estimate batching potential and cache hit rate.

[10:05] Marcus: we have a hard budget for MVP of $25k/month, can Redwood's dedicated pricing be modeled to fit that?
[10:13] Samira: likely yes at certain commit sizes, or blended: small dedicated plus overage. We'll run scenarios: fully hosted to see if volume discounts + caching hits get you under $25k, and dedicated with a 3–6 month commit to see amortized cost. We'll also model a pilot using smaller models or quantized variants to reduce cost.

[10:45] Oliver: what about encryption / KMS — we need customer-managed keys for model snapshots and logs
[10:51] Samira: we support KMS integration on Private and Dedicated; hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys but we can enable Bring-Your-Own-Key for enterprise plans. We'll send the security doc with SOC2, ISO and KMS details.

[11:18] Priya: how do fallbacks work if dedicated capacity is saturated? we need graceful degradation not hard 503s
[11:23] Ethan: we do smart routing and fallback policies — you can configure a policy to failover to hosted model variants or lower-cost models, or to queue. Policies can be per-route with canary thresholds.

[11:50] Marcus: ok good — more practical: can you run a benchmark with our prompt set and show real per-token latency and throughput on a ded pool?
[11:58] Ethan: yes we'd like to do that. typical plan: you share prompt mix and traces, Redwood runs a benchmark on a dedicated-equivalent pool and returns measured QPS, median/tail latency, and cost estimate. That will be our technical deep dive.

[12:22] Samira: timeline check — are you aiming for a pilot in Q2?
[12:26] Oliver: yes target is first pilot by mid-late Q2, internal approvals in next 3–4 weeks

[12:35] Marcus: approvals will hinge on predictable cost and security ok from infra.

[12:42] Samira: action items recap: Samira share cost-model sheet + competitor notes; Ethan schedule benchmark deep dive; Pinelake to send prompt traces and pilot QPS; Samira will also send security/KMS docs.

[12:58] Priya: for deep dive please include a test with quantized model and with and without prefix cache so we can see delta
[13:06] Ethan: noted, we'll include int8 and 4-bit runs and a prefix cache scenario.

[13:22] Marcus: ok thanks, last question: what about rollout? after pilot how do we scale on demand?
[13:29] Samira: Redwood supports autoscaling policies for Dedicated and Hosted, plus burst capacity and fallbacks. For Private we can provide deployment runbooks and autoscale hooks but you'll need to provision infra. We'll include runbook excerpt in the followups.

[13:50] Oliver: perfect. that covers high level, we'll review the sheet and get traces over.

[14:00] Samira: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and a couple proposed times for the deep dive.

End of transcript.
